recordType.value: snapshot, with plaintext account_id set to the owning account

payloadShape.value: { date, value, note }, and no rate field of any kind

decimalScale.value: every quantity is parsed into a BigInt at a fixed scale of 12 decimal places, computed on as an integer, and formatted back to a string. No IEEE-754 float touches a value, a rate or a total, and no decimal library is pulled in

decimalRounding.value: multiplication rescales once, the integer product of two scale-12 values being scale 24 divided back by 10^12 with round-half-even. Addition and subtraction need no rescale. Division happens only in the percentage view and per-account interpolation and rounds half-even at scale 12 as well. Display rounding is a separate later step

valueInputBound.value: a value with more than twelve decimal places is rejected at input rather than silently truncated

dateFormat.value: YYYY-MM-DD, no time and no timezone

uniqueness.value: one snapshot per (account, date), a client-side rule the server cannot see

replacePromptRule.value: the replace prompt fires only where the stored figure is not already displayed in the field being edited, which is the single-holding form at a date the person chose. It does not fire in a reopened recording, and it does not fire in the archive dialog's closing-snapshot field

upsertResult.value: on confirm, the existing record is updated in place: same record_id, version + 1, fresh nonce

confirming.value: confirming writes an ordinary snapshot with the same value, a new date and a new record_id. No new field. It is one click for every kind of account with no branch between them, and it is unavailable for an account with no snapshots

recordingIsDerived.value: a recording is a date and nothing stores it. No fifth record type and no grouping record. It is a client-side index over the in-memory model, grouping snapshots and rate entries by their own date field. It exists exactly as long as a record carries its date, has no version, no author, no wall-clock time and no note of its own

recordingDateIsFixed.value: a recording's date does not move. Moving one entry between dates stays an edit of that snapshot from the holding's own page

openingWritesNothing.value: opening a recording writes nothing and fetches nothing. Not a version bump, not a nonce, not a rate request

createVersusReopen.value: which of the two happens is routing, decided before anything is typed. Asking for a new recording and picking a date the model already holds records for opens that recording's own screen, with no request and nothing created. Editing it is one Update away

preCreateReload.value: before the first record a sitting creates at a date, the client reloads the types it will create in, GET /api/records?type=snapshot and type=rate, and re-checks against freshly reloaded records rather than the model in memory. It runs once per sitting, not once per row. A sitting that creates nothing runs no reload

staleCreateRefusal.value: a save is refused whole when the reload finds the date recorded elsewhere, or finds any slot the save would create already taken. Nothing is written, not even into slots that are still free, and what was typed is lost with no draft buffer, no merge and no re-apply

clearingRule.value: a quantity cleared in a reopened recording deletes that snapshot. Only a field backed by a record at that date can be cleared: emptying a field prefilled from the holding's figure at another date deletes nothing. Clearing a quantity clears no rate. Clearing every quantity leaves the recording with its rates intact. Clearing carries no more confirmation than any other save. A DELETE answering Not Found counts as done

deleteRecording.value: a separate action removes every record bearing that date, snapshots and rate entries together, under one confirmation stating that it is destructive and cannot be restored. Ordinary DELETE requests, quantities first and rates after, with no transaction spanning them. A partial delete leaves a recording, rolls nothing back and marks nothing half-deleted. The date is free afterwards, and this is the only way a date becomes free

dateMoveOrder.value: a date move is a PUT of this record at the new date followed by a DELETE of the record being displaced, in that order. Delete-first risks losing the displaced record while the PUT fails

twoSnapshotsOnOneDate.value: a reachable state, surfaced and never silently resolved. The client picks neither, not by version and not by updated_at, renders both flagged in the account's history and in that date's recording with an action to keep one, and excludes that date from interpolation until resolved

priceNeverBlocksQuantity.value: nothing in the price half ever blocks a quantity, in any form: no disabled save, no required rate field, no warning to dismiss first. This file owns that rule and record-rate.md points at it

dateBounds.value: a future date is blocked. A date preceding the account's createdAt is allowed, because backfilling history is normal

valueRange.value: zero is valid and means a closed-out position, which is not the same as having no snapshot. Negative is valid, because net worth is a signed sum

archivedAccounts.value: an archived account takes no new snapshots, the one exception being the closing snapshot written as part of archiving, dated archivedAt and written in the same flow that sets it

rollbackIsNotDetected.value: the AAD's version binds a ciphertext to the version it was written at but does not prevent a rollback of an intact (ciphertext, version) pair. Do not write a test asserting rollback is detected today

fixtures: a seeded vault of fifteen holdings across six symbols, for the sweep's one-reload and one-rate-request assertions
a decimal midpoint case that sits exactly on the half in both directions, for round-half-even on a scale-12 multiplication

a second session whose in-memory model predates the first session's recording at a date, for the pre-create reload refusal, exercised both as a whole fresh recording and as one holding added inside a reopened one
a date holding a recording, a date holding only rate entries, and a free date, for the routing between create and reopen
a holding whose row on a reopened date is prefilled from its figure at an earlier date, for the clearing rule
a stubbed DELETE that fails, for the write-then-delete order on a date move and for the partial delete of a recording
a stubbed DELETE answering Not Found during a save, which must report as saved
two snapshots planted for one (account, date), for the flagged pair and the interpolation exclusion
an archived account and an account whose archive date already holds a snapshot
focus: a figure the screen pre-filled into a row and nobody confirmed must appear nowhere afterwards. This is the single easiest rule in the product to satisfy on paper and to fake in a test: leave eleven of fifteen rows alone, save, and assert against the holdings' own record sets that no snapshot was created at that date for any of them, rather than against the sweep's own report of what it did

clearing every figure at a date must leave the recording standing with its rate entries byte-identical, and the recording must reopen showing its rate lines. A test that only checks the date still appears in a list proves nothing about the entries

clearing a field prefilled from another date must delete nothing and write nothing. The fake here is a test that clears a field backed by a real record, which passes whatever rule the implementation actually uses

the pre-create reload has to be asserted as a request count and a position: exactly one extra type reload, before the first row is written and none after it, and none at all for a sitting that only changes and clears. Both halves are invisible to an end-state assertion
the refusal of a save whose reload finds the date taken must be shown to have written nothing at all, including into slots that were still free. Checking the error message is the easy fake

the date move must issue the PUT before the DELETE, asserted with the DELETE stubbed to fail so that both records still exist afterwards. An implementation that deletes first passes every happy-path test

round-half-even has to be asserted on a value sitting exactly on the midpoint in both directions. Any other case passes under round-half-up as well, and the rounding mode is what two implementations drift on
a Conflict inside a recording save must reload that row and retry nothing, with the stored record byte-identical afterwards. A retry that happens to succeed looks like correct behaviour

editing inside a reopened recording must never show the replace prompt while the single-holding form at an occupied date still does. Testing only one of the two directions leaves the rule half-asserted
do not write a test asserting that a rolled-back (ciphertext, version) pair is detected. The spec states outright that it is not, and a green test here would be asserting something untrue
